findings.rationale: GenHlth distribution shifts by about 1 federation SD from round 11 and stays there (near 0 before). Local calibration goes negative (CITL about -0.08 at round 20) with high ECE and high O/E in both sex subgroups. Updates become anomalous from round 11: norm ratio rises to about 2.6-3.6 and cosine turns negative. Local AUC and labels look otherwise plausible, so this is a feature drift rather than label or poisoning fault.

GenHlth and HighBP distributions shift by about 1 federation SD from round 11 onward, with near-zero shift before. Mean-shift z of 3.8 and GenHlth z_noise of -5.95 confirm the shift. Local CITL is negative (-0.05, z -4.2) with high O/E in both sex subgroups. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 1.86, min cos -0.69), consistent with the data change.

Feature shift of about 0.9-1.3 SD from round 11 onward, with near-zero shift before round 11 (0.16 at round 10). Mean-shift z of 3.6 and GenHlth z_noise of -6.1. Updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 1.62, min cos -0.73, min_cos z -3.5). Local performance is otherwise fairly normal, so drift is preferred over poisoning.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of the update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup tools, then confirmed suspects with narrower queries. Three clients (GA, WI, UT) show a sustained feature drift in GenHlth (and HighBP for GA/WI) of roughly 1 federation SD starting at round 11, with anomalous updates and, for GA and WI, negative local CITL. I classify them as drift with onset round 11, confidence highest for GA and WI. Not reported: GU shows erratic per-round updates and a size-adjusted norm flag, but it is a small client (n=708) with the noise scaled accordingly, and the budget was exhausted before it could be confirmed; treat as a watch-list item. Other single outliers (NV AgeGroup 5 outcome rate, MA Income 4 O/E, DC BMI, VI HighChol, NC HighChol, GA/WI/UT HighBP tail values) were either noise-scale (z_noise below 4), not replicated on re-query (DC BMI), or from small subgroups. No evidence of label noise, prevalence shift, poisoning, free-riding, subgroup under-diagnosis, or missing-value sentinels was found at the confirmed level. Budget fully spent (20.0 epsilon).
